subject: Anthropology
title: Domestic Mode of Production
description: A fast breakdown of Domestic Mode of Production for builders.

hook.text: Why would a farmer stop planting when he could grow more? Because he has enough. Not every economy seeks surplus.

buildup.text: Sahlins described the domestic mode of production — households producing for their own needs, not for profit or market.

discovery.text: In this system, families produce what they need and stop. There's no drive to accumulate beyond sufficiency.

twist.text: Chiefs and states push production beyond household needs. Surplus doesn't arise naturally — it's demanded by power.

climax.text: The domestic mode shows that overproduction isn't human nature. The drive to produce more is a political creation.

punchline.text: Enough is a revolutionary economic concept.

quiz.question: What is the domestic mode of production?
options: Households producing for their own needs, not for profit

details.summary: Marshall Sahlins's domestic mode of production describes how pre-capitalist households produce primarily for their own consumption rather than for exchange. Households under-produce relative to their capacity because they have no incentive to create surplus beyond immediate needs.
details.whyItMatters: The domestic mode of production challenges the assumption that humans naturally maximize output. Sahlins showed that many societies deliberately limit production.
takeaways: Pre-capitalist households produce for consumption, not exchange
Households under-produce because surplus has no value to them
This challenges assumptions that humans naturally maximize output

faq.question: What is the original affluent society thesis?
faq.answer: Sahlins argued that hunter-gatherers were affluent not because they had much but because they wanted little. Working only 15 to 20 hours per week to meet their needs, they had more leisure than modern workers. Affluence is achievable by desiring less, not just producing more.

faq.question: How does capitalism change the domestic mode of production?
faq.answer: Capitalism forces households into market production by enclosing commons, imposing taxes payable only in money, and creating consumer desires. Once subsistence is no longer possible outside the market, households must produce surplus for exchange rather than for their own consumption.
